newsitem.title: ESTONIA: HANSA AND EMV LEAD SHARES AHEAD OF LONG WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: HANSA AND EMV LEAD SHARES AHEAD OF LONG WEEKEND.

text.p: Share prices on the Estonian
stock exchange were mixed on Friday but the Talse index firmed
slightly.
Dealers said that all eyes were on half-year results and
possible higher profit estimates for the year.
Total turnover on the main list was 46.5 million kroons and
the Talse index gained 0.38 percent to 267.72.
"Hansa and EMV were the most active but with the Nordic
coutries on holidays and Estonia about to go on holidays trade
was slower," one dealer said.
Hansapank was the most active stock with 16 million kroons
traded to gain 0.80 kroons to close at 142.00 kroons.
"Today's trade was normal for the last session before an
extended break but the next two weeks should attract more
interest ahead of the half year bank results," another said.
Dealers and investors are looking forward to mid-July when
banks are expected to report buoyant half-year results.
"The July figures will radically change the market and kick
it off for the autumn season," another trader said.
"Several banks have said they are considering changing their
profit estimates and these will be watched," one dealer said.
The free market saw trade of 17 million kroons with
constuction company EMV the most active stock with an
impressive gain of 6.75 kroons to close on 67.75 kroons.
The gains were made after it released five month results on
Thursday, showing a profit of 7.8 million kroons.
Rakvere was traded up to end at 14.05 kroons, 0.65
kroons higher with 4.4 million kroons traded.
"Rakvere is still a good stock and as it was said, if the
insiders thought it was a good stock then it is most likely
still a good stock," one dealer said.
Rakvere was suspended for one day on Wednesday after the
bourse announced that an insider trading investigation had
started into trade of the company's stock.
-- David Mardiste, Tallinn newsroom, +372 620 9202,
